title: Normalization of the whole-system direct image of an arbitrary reduction
statement: Fix a prime l, a finite extension E of Q_l, schemes X,Y and any morphism f:X→Y. Suppose integralComparisonSequenceDirectImage(f) is additive and coefficientSequenceModules(X) admits K-injective resolutions [def-trf-integral-comparison-sequence-systems, def-coef-ringed-sequence-site]. Let S be a CoefficientDerivedSystemCalculus on X [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus] and K any unbounded derived completed-coefficient complex on X. Then N=R(integralComparisonSequenceDirectImage(f))(S.reduction(K)) is an IsNormalizedCoefficientSequence on Y [def-coef-ringed-sequence-site]: for all n≤m and P in D(B_n), precomposition with its actual derived transition N_m→Res(N_n) bijects Hom(N_n,P) with Hom(N_m,Res(P)). This asserts no comparison of total limits or Roos projections.

source.place: Construction 4.1 and Lemma 4.10; combined with the perfect-quotient argument of Bhatt--Scholze Lemma 6.5.11(3), Stacks 0941 and 099N.

proof.text: Resolve S.reduction(K) once on the sequence site. Apply the section-normalized derived direct-image evaluation comparison. Compose its nth component with finite direct image of S.reductionEvaluation to identify N_n with Rf_*(K tensor^L B_n). The arbitrary-resolution normalization and the restriction-transition equation ensure compatibility with every quotient map.

source.place: Construction 4.1 and Lemma 4.10; combined with the perfect-quotient argument of Bhatt--Scholze Lemma 6.5.11(3), Stacks 0941 and 099N.

proof.text: Each B_n has its two-term free resolution over completed coefficients. Apply the perfect-quotient projection formula to identify Rf_*(K tensor^L B_n) with (Rf_*K) tensor^L B_n. Use the normalized restriction comparison to compare their quotient transitions. On the two-term resolutions B_m→B_n is identity in degree zero and multiplication by the intervening uniformizer power in degree minus one; naturality of the derived direct-image unit gives precisely the actual system transitions.

source.place: Construction 4.1 and Lemma 4.10; combined with the perfect-quotient argument of Bhatt--Scholze Lemma 6.5.11(3), Stacks 0941 and 099N.

proof.text: Derived scalar-extension associativity identifies the transition-adjoint for the resulting reduction tower with (Rf_*K tensor^L B_m) tensor^L_(B_m) B_n→Rf_*K tensor^L B_n, an isomorphism. Transport to N. The scalar adjunction converts its invertibility into the required Hom-set bijection. Identity quotients, positive exponent one, zero inputs and empty schemes satisfy the same equations.

theorem systemDirectImage_reduction_normalized
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    [(integralComparisonSequenceDirectImage l E f).Additive]
    [Abelian.HasKInjectiveResolutions (coefficientSequenceModules l E X)]
    (S : CoefficientDerivedSystemCalculus l E X)
    (K : DerivedCategory (scalarReductionSource l E X)) :
    IsNormalizedCoefficientSequence l E Y
      ((integralComparisonSequenceDirectImage l E f).rightDerivedFunctor.obj
        (S.reduction.obj K))
